slides.say: Data Science from Scratch, lesson fifteen: why Python for data science.

slides.text: Spreadsheets get you far. Why code?
slides.say: Spreadsheets can take you surprisingly far. So why do most data scientists learn to code, and why is Python such a common choice?

slides.text: Python reads almost like plain English
slides.say: First, Python is known for being readable. Its code often looks close to plain English, which makes it a friendly first language.
Second, its libraries. pandas handles tables, NumPy handles fast maths on arrays, Matplotlib draws charts, and scikit-learn gives you many standard machine learning models.

slides.text: Code is a recipe you can rerun
slides.sub: New data next month? Run it again.
slides.say: Third, code is repeatable. A script is a recipe: when new data arrives next month, you run the same steps again, and anyone can check exactly what you did.
And Python is free and open source, with a large community, so when you get stuck, someone has usually asked the same question before.

slides.text: Python isn't the only option, but it's a strong first one
slides.say: So the takeaway: Python isn't the only option. R and SQL are useful too. But it's a strong first language for data science.
Next lesson: meet the pandas DataFrame.

summary: Python is a popular first language for data science because it is readable, free, and has strong libraries like pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib and scikit-learn. Code also makes your analysis repeatable.
practice: Think of one task you repeat in a spreadsheet every week or month. Write down, step by step in plain English, what you do — that list is the start of a script.
